title: token-throughput-slew-hosted-dedicated-private
creator: Marisol Ortega
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent first-token and sustained tokens/sec regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments starting 2025-11-02. Symptoms: TTFT spikes (200-1,200ms above baseline) and sustained token/sec drop (~30-60%) on mid-length conversations (200-800 tokens). Affected models: quantized int8 variants and a subset of fp16 kernels under certain sequence-length mixes. Impacted workloads include streaming chat, long-format completion, and batch reranking.

Observed behavior and scope:
- Occurs in US-EAST and EU-WEST regions primarily, with isolated Private/VPC reports from two customers.
- Pattern is intermittent and correlates with model fanout and heterogeneous context windows.
- Telemetry shows elevated kernel preemption counts and KV cache eviction churn before TTFT spikes.

Initial hypothesis: A regression in the kernel-selector heuristic introduced in runtime-1.20 causes suboptimal kernel paths for models with mixed context-length distributions. Under load this triggers eviction races in the per-worker kernel cache and a timing window where the quantized int8 kernel requires a slow fallback or recompilation, causing token emission delays and throughput collapse.

Why urgent: Customers are experiencing SLA violations and degraded UX; several PM/CS escalations are open. Reproducible in staging with a synthetic mix that mirrors the production distribution.

Reproduction steps (staging):
1) Deploy model variants: model-A-int8 (quantized), model-A-fp16 (fallback).
2) Pump mixed-length request stream (10% short, 70% mid 200-600 tokens, 20% long) at baseline throughput.
3) Observe kernel-selector toggles and KV cache thrash in /metrics/runtime/kernel_* and TTFT spikes in /dashboards/ttft_over_time.

Proposed short-term mitigations implemented:
- Rolled feature flag to disable new kernel-selector heuristic in affected regions (feature-flag: kernel_selector_v2 -> off).
- Deployed emergency routing policy to prefer fp16-compatible kernels for affected models while keeping int8 available as a lower-priority variant. (routing change live: 2025-11-04 03:12 UTC)
- Tightened KV cache eviction to deterministic LRU for hot contexts to reduce thrash (config patch: runtime-kv-evict=v0.9-rollout).
- Adjusted hedged-warmstart to aggressive prefetch for multi-tenant hot sessions (config: hedged_warmstart.backoff=50ms).
- Added temporary alerting thresholds for kernel_preempt_count and kv_eviction_rate to trigger automated rollback.

Work completed so far:
- 2025-11-03 18:34 UTC: Incident bridge created and customer-communication thread opened (Slack #incident-ttft-slew).
- 2025-11-04 03:12 UTC: Kernel-selector v2 toggled off in US-EAST and EU-WEST (canary -> regional rollout).
- 2025-11-04 08:47 UTC: Routing policy change applied; immediate partial recovery observed in hosted clusters (~15-25% token/sec improvement).
- 2025-11-05 01:20 UTC: Deterministic KV eviction deployed to staging and hotfix queued for canary.
- 2025-11-06 22:05 UTC: Private customer workarounds documented and shared with affected accounts; CS and AMs notified (email thread and support tickets linked).

Planned long-term fix:
- Address race in kernel cache eviction and kernel selector by implementing deterministic kernel residency tracking and a lightweight kernel warm-up handshake to avoid recompilation in fast paths.
- Add per-model sequence-length histograms to routing heuristics so models choose the most robust kernel under their workload distribution.
- Increase test coverage with large-scale synthetic mixes in CI and nightly soak tests across hosted/dedicated/private.

Criteria for close:
- TTFT return to baseline (within 15%) for 7 consecutive days across regions and deployments.
- No customer escalations for the same root cause after fallbacks are removed for 72 hours.
- CR: Merge and rollout of runtime fix and a follow-up postmortem published.

Notes and customer comms:
- Severity: S1; external communication sent 2025-11-04 09:05 UTC.
- Affected accounts: ACME Finance (Dedicated), NovaHealth (Private), three Hosted trial orgs.
- Suggested messaging: acknowledge impact, describe mitigations, ETA for stable fix and offer dedicated post-incident review.
